landmarks.name: Registan Square
landmarks.writeup: A historic public square in Samarkand, surrounded by three madrasahs showcasing Timurid architecture.

wiki.extract: Registan, officially the Registan Square is a historic public square in the city of Samarkand, Uzbekistan. It served as the heart of the Timurid Empire and later as the city's commercial, educational, and ceremonial center. The square is famed for its ensemble of three madrasas : the Ulugh Beg Madrasa of the Timurid period, the Sherdar Madrasa and the Tilakari Madrasa, built later under the Janid dynasty—which together they represent some of the finest achievements of Islamic architecture in Central Asia. Renowned for its soaring iwans, turquoise domes, intricate mosaic tilework, and geometric ornamentation, Registan is considered one of the greatest examples of Timurid and Persian-influenced architecture..

landmarks.name: Itchan Kala
landmarks.writeup: The walled inner town of Khiva, a UNESCO World Heritage site with well-preserved Islamic architecture.

wiki.extract: Itchan Kala is the walled inner town of the city of Khiva, Uzbekistan. Since 1990, it has been protected as a World Heritage Site.

landmarks.name: Bukhara Historic Centre
landmarks.writeup: An ancient city center with numerous mosques, madrasahs, and bazaars reflecting Central Asian culture.

wiki.extract: Bukhara is the seventh-largest city in Uzbekistan by population, with 280,187 residents as of 1 January 2020. It is the capital of Bukhara Region.

cultural_events.name: Navruz
cultural_events.writeup: The Persian New Year celebrated on March 21, marking the beginning of spring with traditional music, dance, and food.

cultural_events.name: Sharq Taronalari
cultural_events.writeup: An international music festival held in Samarkand, celebrating traditional and contemporary music from Central Asia.

wiki.extract: Sharq taronalari is UNESCO listed international music festival that is held in every two years since 1997 in Registan square of ancient Samarkand. Vocalists from different nations and countries participate in the festival.

food_writeup: Uzbek cuisine features hearty dishes such as plov (rice pilaf with meat and vegetables), shashlik (grilled meat skewers), and samsa (savory pastries), reflecting a blend of Central Asian flavors.
brief_history: Uzbekistan, historically part of the Silk Road, was ruled by various empires including the Persian Empire, Alexander the Great, and the Timurid dynasty. It became a Soviet republic in 1924 and gained independence in 1991 after the USSR's dissolution.

important_people.description: 14th-century conqueror and founder of the Timurid Empire

current_conflicts: Uzbekistan is generally stable with no active internal or external conflicts, focusing on regional cooperation and economic development.

commentary.inflation_management: Uzbekistan's inflation was chronically high under the old closed regime, 11-14% through 2006-16, reflecting the overvalued official exchange rate and administered prices. The September 2017 liberalization, which devalued the sum by roughly half and unified exchange rates, pushed inflation to 13.9% in 2017 and 17.5% in 2018; it has since moderated to a projected 8.8% in 2025 as the central bank adopted inflation targeting (2020) and tightened credibly. Dollar-term GDP fell from $97.3bn (2016) to $61.3bn (2018) on the devaluation before recovering to a projected $147.1bn in 2025. The disinflation path is real but incomplete.
commentary.debt_management: Public debt was minimal under Karimov (5-12% of GDP through 2016) because the state barely borrowed externally. Liberalization changed this: the ratio rose to 17.3% in 2017, 24.3% in 2019, and 31.9% in 2020 as the government borrowed for reforms and COVID, stabilizing at a projected 28.6% in 2025. The increase is deliberate and still moderate; most borrowing is concessional. The risk is state-enterprise and PPP contingent liabilities accumulating opaquely as the investment drive continues.

key_events.event: Karimov died after 27 years; Mirziyoyev succeeded and launched reforms.
Foreign-exchange liberalization: sum devalued ~50%, convertibility restored.
Tax reform and WTO-accession drive; Tashkent opened to investors.
COVID-19; Uzbekistan borrowed to fund health and social spending.
Karakalpakstan unrest over constitutional changes; autonomy retained.
Constitutional referendum extended presidential terms; reform momentum questioned.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: Uzbekistan's base case is 5-6% growth on reforms, demographics, and investment, with inflation converging toward target and debt staying moderate. The reform story is genuine but incomplete: state dominance, corruption, and water/energy constraints (notably the Aral Sea legacy) persist. Risks are reform reversal, regional instability, and over-borrowing for mega-projects. Analytical assessment: the most promising reform trajectory in Central Asia, but the 2017-19 momentum needs sustaining to deliver.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
